name: Nevquo Request a Quote for WooCommerce
author: nevquo

sections.description:
Customers click “Request a quote” on a product, fill in a short form, and you get an email. The request also lands in WooCommerce > Quotes, where you can set a status, reply to the customer, and keep private notes.

  • Button on single product pages, with an optional link on shop and category pages
  • Works for simple and variable products (customers pick the option)
  • Show it on every product, or only on the products you tick
  • Optional quote-only mode that hides “Add to cart” on those products
  • Six statuses: New, In review, Quoted, Accepted, Declined, Closed
  • Replies are emailed to the customer; private notes stay in the admin
  • Email to you for each new request, optional confirmation copy to the customer
  • Search, filter by status, sort and bulk-update from the list
  • Spam protection without CAPTCHA: honeypot field and a per-visitor hourly limit
  • Works with page caching (no nonce in the public form)
  • Supports WordPress personal data export and erase
  • Compatible with HPOS; loads its CSS and JS only on pages that show a quote button
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip from Plugins > Add New > Upload.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Settings > Quotes and check where the button should appear and who gets the emails.
  4. Visit a product page. The button is already there.

Requests arrive under WooCommerce > Quotes.
sections.faq:
The button doesn’t show up.

Check WooCommerce > Settings > Quotes > Show on. If it is set to “Only products I tick”, tick “Quote button” under Product data > General on the product. External and grouped products never show the button. Block themes: the button is added after the Add to Cart form block; if your template doesn’t use that block, place the shortcode [wcrq_button] where you want it.

Emails don’t arrive.

The plugin uses wp_mail(), the same as the rest of WordPress. If your host doesn’t deliver PHP mail reliably, install an SMTP plugin. When a reply can’t be sent, the quote screen marks it “Email not sent” and leaves the status alone so you can try again.

The form says it couldn’t reach the server.

The form posts to /wp-json/wcrq/v1/quotes. Some security plugins block the REST API for logged-out visitors. Allow that route.

Can customers reply by email and have it show in the quote?

No. Replies go to the Reply-To address in the settings, and you continue from your inbox. Use “Save as private note” to record what was agreed.

How do I translate the button and form text?

The button label, intro text and consent text are settings. With WPML they appear under String Translation (domain nevquo-request-a-quote). Everything else uses standard WordPress translation files.

How do I change how the form looks?

Override the CSS variables on .wcrq-dialog (accent colour, radius) from your theme. To change the markup, copy templates/form.php or templates/email.php into your-theme/nevquo-request-a-quote/.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing, unless you tick “Delete all quotes and settings when the plugin is deleted” in the Quotes settings. Deactivating never deletes anything.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • The per-visitor hourly limit now counts requests atomically, so simultaneous requests can’t slip past it.
  • Output escaping is applied at the point of output in every template and screen.

1.0.1

  • The quote form no longer closes when you click outside it or finish a text selection outside the box. Use the X, Cancel or Esc.

1.0.0

  • First release.
